CZ construction SMBs run on spreadsheets and Pohoda; Stavario covers site diaries/attendance, nothing spans procurement-to-invoicing.
notes:
- Model: construction-firm back-office OS, DE-proven fresh funding.
- CZ transfer logic: same fragmented mid-size construction sector; partial incumbent Stavario (site diary, attendance) named — not an integrated ops platform.
- Relevance: arbitrage receipt for p-0007 (construction subcontractor management / construction firm ops).

title: Exnaton — white-label energy-community billing
summary: Model proven abroad: Exnaton (ETH spin-off, DACH) sells white-label billing and settlement SaaS for energy communities and P2P electricity sharing, used by utilities across DACH/Nordics; quick search found no CZ equivalent even though CZ sdílení elektřiny via EDC launched Aug 2024 and communities reportedly lose up to half of shared electricity to bad allocation/settlement.
notes:
- Model: SaaS for energetická společenství: member billing, allocation keys, settlement against DSO/market data; DACH-proven (Exnaton; Austrian peers eFriends/OurPower prove community-energy tooling demand under EU RED II).
- CZ transfer logic: Lex OZE II enabled komunitní energetika from 2024; EDC handles data exchange but not community admin, member billing or optimization; HN (2025) reports communities losing up to ~50% of shared electricity value — an acute tooling gap; municipalities founding společenství have zero software.
- Absence check (2026-08-13): searches return EDC itself, ministry PR and ASITIS (consulting/services); no dedicated CZ community-energy billing/settlement SaaS. Classification: weak incumbent (consultancies), timely regulatory window.

title: Fuchs & Eule — AI building-retrofit analytics
summary: Fuchs & Eule (Berlin) raised €10M (GET Fund, 8 Jul 2026) for AI building-retrofit analytics — screens commercial landlord/asset-manager portfolios for ESG and energy-retrofit needs; 10,000 building analyses done. Czech landlords face the same EPBD/ESG retrofit pressure with only consultancies (PKV Build does certificates at scale) — no self-serve analytics software.
notes:
- Model: portfolio-level retrofit analytics for building owners.
- CZ transfer logic: EPBD recast infringement pressure (reg-epbd-recast) forces the CZ implementing law onto a compressed timeline; commercial portfolios need triage tooling before capex.
- Relevance: primary arbitrage receipt for a new EPBD-retrofit-analytics problem, paired with reg-epbd-recast.

title: JUPUS — AI secretarial layer for law firms
summary: JUPUS (Cologne) raised €13M Series A (Semapa Next, 23 Jun 2026) for an AI secretarial layer for law firms — AI phone assistant for client intake, case structuring, document drafting; 2,000+ lawyers, ~70 h/month saved per firm. CZ has practice management (SingleCase) and document automation (Legito) but no AI intake/phone layer for the ~13k solo and small advokát practices.
notes:
- Status: watch signal — held as candidate-problem material; needs a CZ demand receipt (advokát complaints, ČAK surveys) before a problem record is opened.
- Named CZ partial incumbents: SingleCase (practice mgmt), Legito (doc automation) — neither does intake automation.

title: Skalar — AI-native tax & accounting firm
summary: Skalar (Munich, by Stocard's founder) raised a €12M seed (Headline, 14 Jul 2026) for an AI-native tax and accounting firm — AI agents do bookkeeping/payroll/tax grunt work so one professional serves 100+ clients, attacking Germany's tax-advisor shortage. CZ has the same accountant shortage; Digitoo automates invoice capture and ÚOL sells online accounting, but nobody runs a full-stack AI-first advisory firm.
notes:
- Model: AI-first professional-services firm (not SaaS) — the labor-shortage arbitrage.
- CZ transfer logic: accountant shortage + nový zákon o účetnictví (reg-accounting-act-cz, planned 2028) create a re-platforming moment; incumbents are practice software vendors, not service disruptors.
- Relevance: primary arbitrage receipt for a new accounting-capacity problem.

title: VARM — tech-enabled insulation installer
summary: VARM (Berlin) raised €17.5M Series A (ABN AMRO Sustainable Impact Fund, 23 Jun 2026) as a tech-enabled insulation installer: trains career-changers as certified installers and insulates a family home in one day at a fixed ~€5k price. CZ mirrors Germany — NZÚ subsidies plus a long tail of one-man insulation firms; Woltair proved the vertical-installer model here for heat pumps/PV but nobody does insulation.
notes:
- Model: tech-enabled trade execution (Woltair-for-insulation), not SaaS.
- CZ transfer logic: identical subsidy structure (NZÚ covers zateplení), identical fragmentation; the trained-installer supply model attacks the real constraint (labor).
- Relevance: primary arbitrage receipt for a new insulation-retrofit-execution problem.

title: Festina Finance — pension & life-insurance platform
summary: Festina Finance (Copenhagen) raised €25M+ growth (Birchway Capital, ~€200M valuation, 19 Jun 2026) for a cloud-native modular platform modernizing pension and life-insurance administration — 10M policies across 4 countries. Czech pension reform (DIP since 2024) is forcing penzijní společnosti and life insurers off legacy cores; no local modern platform vendor, only SI body-shops (Adastra, Sabris).
notes: - Status: watch signal — enterprise sales motion makes this consultancy/dev-shop territory; revisit if a DIP-driven modernization tender or ČNB pressure surfaces.

title: sunbay.io — AI receivables & dunning automation
summary: sunbay.io (Warsaw) raised €550k pre-seed (Kogito Ventures + s20, 11 Jun 2026) for AI receivables/dunning automation — plugs into the accounting system and chases overdue invoices via email/SMS/voice with escalation logic. Czech SMBs suffer long payment delays with only manual inkaso agencies and Fakturoid's basic reminders; Digitoo covers payables, nobody does AI receivables.
notes: - Status: watch signal — small round, but PL-market proof directly adjacent to CZ; pairs with the SMB cash-flow pain documented in p-0005/p-0010 bodies. Needs a CZ demand receipt before a problem record.

title: autarc — OS for heat-pump & solar installers
summary: Model proven abroad: autarc (YC S24, Berlin, ~30 people) is the agentic OS for heat-pump/solar installation companies — heat-load calc, quoting, subsidy paperwork, project management on one platform; quick search found no CZ equivalent, only manufacturers' sizing tools and the installers themselves.
notes:
- Model: vertical SaaS for energy installers (heat pumps, PV): digital site survey, heat load calculation, quote generation, subsidy application handling, install project tracking. Germany-proven where installer workflows and subsidy bureaucracy mirror CZ.
- CZ transfer logic: Nová zelená úsporám drives tens of thousands of heat-pump/FVE installs per year executed by hundreds of small montážní firmy drowning in paperwork; Woltair is a vertically integrated installer, not a software vendor to the long tail.
- Absence check (2026-08-13): CZ searches surface only manufacturer configurators (Master Therm) and installation companies; no installer-ops SaaS. Classification: no CZ player found.

title: CoCrafter — contractor-to-subcontractor marketplace
summary: Model proven abroad: CoCrafter (YC W24, Munich) does a B2B marketplace matching general contractors with vetted subcontractors, 3,000+ German SMB companies onboard; quick search found no CZ B2B equivalent — only consumer home-services marketplaces (Wilio, Nejřemeslníci) as weak incumbents.
notes:
- Model: two-sided B2B marketplace for GC-subcontractor matching incl. foreign subcontractor sourcing and document/compliance management; proven in the culturally similar German SMB construction sector.
- CZ transfer logic: CZ construction is subcontractor-driven and suffers chronic labor shortage; sourcing of Ukrainian/Balkan crews is informal (Facebook groups, brokers) with zero vetting or compliance tooling.
- Absence check (2026-08-13): Tracxn CZ construction-tech lists and searches show no B2B subcontractor marketplace; only consumer-facing craftsmen marketplaces. Classification: weak incumbent (consumer-grade only).

title: Gale — corporate work-visa automation
summary: Model proven abroad: Gale (YC W25) automates the corporate work-visa pipeline — application prep, compliance, HR-system integration — coordinating independent attorneys; quick search found no CZ equivalent for zaměstnanecké karty, only form-help site permit.cz and classic law firms as weak incumbents.
notes:
- Model: software layer that automates employer-sponsored immigration paperwork and compliance; Mayflower (YC F25, HR immigration screening) and LegalOS (W26, AI immigration law firm) show the cluster is hot.
- CZ transfer logic: CZ employers depend on foreign workers (Ukraine, Philippines, India — government kvóty programs); zaměstnanecká karta process is notoriously slow and paper-based; relocation agencies work manually at high fees.
- Absence check (2026-08-13): searches surface ministry pages, law firms (ARROWS) and permit.cz (static form-filling guides). No automation platform. Classification: weak incumbent.

title: Hammr — construction payroll, HR & compliance
summary: Model proven abroad: Hammr (YC W23) does construction-specific payroll, HR and compliance ('Rippling for construction'); quick search found no CZ equivalent — only generic legacy payroll (Vema, Pamica) and site-diary/attendance tools like Stavario as weak incumbents.
notes:
- Model: vertical payroll + HR + compliance built for construction crews (certified payroll, prevailing wage, multi-site time tracking tied to pay).
- CZ transfer logic: CZ construction employs ~400k, heavy subcontracting, agenturní zaměstnávání and A1/posted-worker compliance; payroll handled by generic legacy software or external accountants.
- Absence check (2026-08-13): CZ searches surface site-management tools (Stavario, PlanRadar) and generic payroll (Vema, KS program) — no construction-vertical payroll/compliance product. Classification: weak incumbent.

title: Hemut — AI back office for trucking
summary: Model proven abroad: Hemut (YC Spring 2025) is an AI operating system for trucking companies — AI phone agents, document ingestion, load sourcing, automated accounting; quick search found no CZ equivalent, only legacy TMS/dispečink software as weak incumbents.
notes:
- Model: AI back-office for small/mid trucking firms (calls, POD/document data entry, invoicing/factoring workflows); adjacent YC signals Dayjob (S26, AI scheduling for short-haul) and Peer (S26, AI freight brokerage) confirm the cluster.
- CZ transfer logic: road freight is one of the largest CZ sectors (~40k dopravci, mostly <10 trucks) running on phones, e-mail and legacy TMS; driver shortage and thin margins reward back-office automation; Timocom/Trans.eu cover load boards, not ops.
- Absence check (2026-08-13): searches return only US AI-dispatch tools; CZ side shows legacy dispatch/TMS products, no AI-native ops player. Classification: weak incumbent (legacy TMS).

title: LegalOS — AI-native immigration law firm
summary: LegalOS (YC Winter 2026): 'The AI-Native Immigration Law Firm' — AI-first service model for immigration casework. Direct analog for automating the CZ zaměstnanecká karta process currently run by manual relocation agencies and law firms.
notes: - Relevance: supporting receipt for p-0009 (employment-card automation) — an AI-first service firm (not just software) is the model most transferable to the CZ paper-based visa process.

title: Mercura — AI quote & order processing for distributors
summary: Model proven abroad: Mercura (YC W25, Bavaria, ~20 people) automates quote and order processing for construction-supply distributors and manufacturers with AI; quick search found no CZ equivalent — only global tools and generic automation agencies, no CZ vertical player.
notes:
- Model: AI extraction of inbound RFQs/orders (e-mail, PDF, Excel) into ERP quotes for distributors; Comena (YC S25) and Seals AI (S24) prove the same wedge; Germany-proven in construction supply, directly adjacent to CZ market structure.
- CZ transfer logic: CZ is dense with SMB velkoobchody and manufacturing suppliers running Pohoda/Helios/ABRA ERPs with manual order entry; German-owned distributors in CZ already know the category.
- Absence check (2026-08-13): searches return US/global tools (WizCommerce, turian) and CZ generic AI agencies (Appmine); no CZ product. Classification: no CZ player found.

title: Oma Care — family caregivers, trained and paid
summary: Model proven abroad: Oma Care (YC W24) builds infrastructure to train and get family caregivers paid (53M in the US); quick search found no CZ equivalent navigating příspěvek na péči for families — only static info portals (pece.cz, mpsv.gov.cz guides) as weak incumbents.
notes:
- Model: tech platform that helps family caregivers access state caregiving money, get trained and get support; CareOasis (YC S23) is the same model — a validated US cluster.
- CZ transfer logic: příspěvek na péči (four levels, raised again in 2024-25) flows to ~380k dependent persons, largely spent on informal family care; application, hodnocení stupně závislosti and appeals are bureaucratic and opaque — exactly the navigation layer Oma Care monetizes.
- Absence check (2026-08-13): searches return only advice articles and government pages explaining the benefit; no startup that files, tracks or optimizes claims for families. Classification: no CZ player found (info portals only).

title: PermitPortal — AI pre-construction & permits
summary: Model proven abroad: PermitPortal (YC F24) does an AI operating system for pre-construction — site entitlements, zoning intelligence and permit navigation for developers; quick search found no CZ equivalent, while the state's own digitalizace stavebního řízení remains dysfunctional a year after launch.
notes:
- Model: AI workflows for developers from site sourcing through entitlements to building permit; adjacent YC models Permitify (W25, plan review vs. building code) and Verdant (S26, land-use permits for local gov) prove the cluster.
- CZ transfer logic: CZ has among the slowest building-permit processes in the OECD; the July 2024 DSŘ digitalization fiasco (portál stavebníka) created acute pain for both stavebníci and úřady; new stavební zákon changed procedures.
- Absence check (2026-08-13): searches return news about the broken state system (archiweb: "digitalization stabilized after a year, but still faces complications") and US tools (CivCheck); no CZ startup automating permit prep/navigation. Classification: no CZ player found.

title: Sage Care — AI ops for home-care agencies
summary: Model proven abroad: Sage Care (YC S24) automates home-care agency operations with AI — intake, communication and scheduling busywork; quick search found no CZ equivalent, only the legacy record-keeping system Cygnus DP (IRESOFT) as a weak incumbent for domácí péče agencies.
notes:
- Model: AI-native ops layer (intake calls, client onboarding, coordination) for home-care agencies; sister signals in same YC cluster: Cova (S26, AI-native home care agency) — the model is being replicated, not a one-off.
- CZ transfer logic: hundreds of agentury domácí péče and pečovatelské služby (Včelka, charity providers) run on phone + paper + Cygnus DP record-keeping; chronic nurse shortage makes admin-time savings directly convert to capacity.
- Absence check (2026-08-13): CZ searches return only care providers themselves and IRESOFT Cygnus DP (documentation/billing records, no AI ops automation). Classification: weak incumbent.

title: Sanvivo — e-commerce layer for independent pharmacies
summary: Model proven abroad: Sanvivo (YC W23, Munich) is 'Shopify for pharmacies' — online ordering, advice and click-and-collect infrastructure for independent European pharmacies; quick search found no CZ tool serving independents, who are being squeezed by Dr.Max/BENU/Pilulka chains (weak position, no digital enabler).
notes:
- Model: white-label e-commerce + services layer that lets independent local pharmacies compete with chains online; Remedy (YC F25, AI agents for pharmacies) extends the cluster.
- CZ transfer logic: IQVIA/pharmaboardroom document rapid chain consolidation and e-commerce shift in CZ pharmacy; ~1,000+ remaining independent lékárny have no shared digital storefront; eRecept infrastructure makes digital pickup flows feasible.
- Absence check (2026-08-13): searches return chain e-shops (Pilulka, Dr.Max) and market reports; no digitalization platform for independents. Classification: no CZ player found for the independent segment (chains are incumbent but not the same model).
- Caveat: chain dominance shrinks the addressable independent base — validate segment size before promoting to a problem.
